scene: Original procedural terrain, same packed geometry, same camera, both face-culling disabled

measurement.each_backend: 40 CPU/browser-frame warmup + 120 browser-frame samples, followed by 24 independent asynchronous GPU pass queries
measurement.scope: GPU pass/GL time elapsed for own render invocation, not total frame, GPU utilization or end-to-end runtime
measurement.status: both timer query features available and all GPU samples read successfully

limitations: One session per geometry density; independent repeated trials still required to establish confidence intervals.
WebGL2 timed scope includes GL clear, draw and state changes; WebGPU timestampWrites span an individual render pass and may not include all identical API overhead.
Browser launched with explicit experimental/unsafe WebGPU flags; standard end-user availability must be verified separately.
Graphics adapter timing granularity and timestamp quantization can differ.
Single indexed terrain mesh and modest 697x300 viewport do not represent multi-material, shadowed, animated 3D games.
Browser chrome was headless; real foreground rendering, thermals, and other GPU workloads may differ.
Timing is GPU pass duration, not frame presentation latency, total end-to-end game frame or VRAM pressure.
Do not infer WebGPU is universally faster from these p50/p95 observations.
rights: Original public educational experiment; no private models, user identifiers, file paths, secrets or third-party assets included
